description: heyy, I am Aknur , you can call me Ray!
summary: Earth System Trend Detective answers a simple question: is it really changing? Climate charts are full of seasons and noise, so it is hard to tell a real trend from chance. Our web tool lets anyone pick a question and a place on a 3D map of Kazakhstan, then tests NASA satellite and model data (MERRA-2, GPM IMERG, GLDAS, OMI) from 1980 to 2025. It removes the seasonal cycle, runs Mann-Kendall and Sen’s slope tests corrected for autocorrelation, and returns a plain-language verdict: confirmed, probable or not proven yet, with the size of the change and its caveats. We confirmed widespread warming (+0.17 °C per decade, with half of the country significantly warming), rising evapotranspiration at Lake Balkhash and rising dust near the Aral Sea. We also flag where datasets disagree, such as MERRA-2 versus satellite rainfall, so users know how far to trust each answer.
details:
What it does. The site guides users from a question, to a place, to an answer. Each answer shows a verdict, the trend per decade with its confidence range, and the caveats. Maps mark only cells that stay significant after correcting for testing 2,046 cells at once.

Benefits and intended impact. It helps citizens, journalists, farmers and planners tell real change from noise, and it builds trust by stating uncertainty openly.

Tools. Python (NumPy, SciPy, xarray, pyMannKendall, Matplotlib, earthaccess) for the data pipeline and statistics. HTML, JavaScript and three.js for the 3D map. Data from NASA Giovanni and GES DISC. Code on GitHub: [your repo link]. No special hardware.

Creativity and factors considered. We validated the method on 400 synthetic trendless series: our false-positive rate is 4.8% versus 13.8% for a naive test. We cross-check model against satellite, and we warn that MERRA-2 rainfall is probably inflated and that our warming rate is about half the station value from Kazhydromet.

Use of AI. The presentation slides and README were drafted with AI assistance (Claude).
dataRefs: MERRA-2 Monthly Single-Level Diagnostics, M2TMNXSLV (air temperature)
GPM IMERG Final Run Monthly V07, GPM_3IMERGM (satellite rainfall)
GLDAS Noah Land Surface Model Monthly V2.1, GLDAS_NOAH025_M (soil moisture, evapotranspiration, snow)
OMI/Aura NO2 Cloud-Screened Level 3 V3, OMNO2d (Almaty NO₂)
